questions.stem: A project's window is 2029 to 2031 and its work takes two years, in a plan whose last year is 2031. For which start years does steps/02 create a variable?

options.text: 2029, 2030 and 2031, since each year of the window gets a variable
options.says: The window is cut so the work ends inside the plan; a 2031 start would run into 2032.

options.text: 2029 only, since a window keeps only its first year as a start
options.says: Every year of the cut window gets a variable, not only the first.

options.text: None, since a window that reaches the last year is dropped whole
options.says: The window is cut, not dropped; 2029 and 2030 remain.

options.text: 2029 and 2030, since the work of a 2031 start would end after 2031
options.says: Right: request.starts cuts the window so that the work ends inside the plan's years.

origin.section: A Start-Year Variable per Project and Year Carries the When

questions.stem: A five-year plan built with one envelope fits its total budget. Finance finds it over budget in the first year. Why could the step-01 code not see that?

options.text: Its model has a row per year but adds the years together first
options.says: The step-01 model has one row, `budget`; there is no row per year.

options.text: No year has its own limit, and no cost is tied to a year of work
options.says: Right: Request held one number for money and Project one number for cost.

options.text: Its model has yearly budgets, but the export lacks cost profiles
options.says: The export always carried cost profiles; the step-01 loader did not read them.

options.text: Its model spreads costs, but charges them all to the latest start
options.says: The step-01 model has no years at all, so it spreads nothing.

origin.section: The One-Envelope Plan Overspends the First Year

questions.stem: In steps/02 a project can start in 2027 or in 2030, and either start fits every budget. Which start does the model prefer?

options.text: Neither, since the project's value is the same for every start year
options.says: Right: the objective values a late start the same as an early one, so the solver is free to pick either.

options.text: 2027, since an early start has the higher NPV in finance's export
options.says: Step 02 does not read the NPV by start year; every start is worth the earliest-start value.

options.text: 2030, since a late start leaves the early money for other projects
options.says: Both starts fit, so nothing in the model rewards leaving money early.

options.text: 2027, since the solver tries the earliest start variable first
options.says: The page says the solver is free to push a start late; seven projects started late on GridCap small.

origin.section: Every Year Now Fits, and Some Projects Start Late for No Reason
